transcript: Does an El Niño winter say how much the next fire season will burn?
Seven regions, from Alaska to Southern California.
The idea: after an El Niño winter the north runs milder and often drier, the south wetter.
AK, YT and NorCal are filed separately for not fitting cleanly into either group.
I fixed 52 tests in writing before opening any fire data, then ran them once.
What El Niño does to winter rain. December to February precipitation, as a share of each region’s average winter. Each row is scaled to its own largest swing.
Every fire season since 1984. A shaded year follows an El Niño winter.
Burned area, as a multiple of each region’s typical season, on a log scale. Each row is scaled to its own largest swing.
0 of the 25 tests that set El Niño against burned area are significant. Every interval crosses zero.
4 of 52 tests are significant after correcting for the number of tests. These are associations, not causes.
The whiplash index: each year’s summer water balance minus its winter water balance. SPEI-3 JJA minus DJF, in standard deviations (SD). A description; it was not tested.
A wet winter changes what burns in only some places: more the next year in Northern California, less the same year in Alberta.
A forecast for 2027 goes up before the season and is checked against it afterwards.
